Desk cover evening rules

Purpose: to keep Companion Animal Travel Desk handovers calm, accurate, and kind while we support pets and travelers through every step of the journey.

When you take over desk cover, start by checking the active files, the waiting messages, and any notes left by the earlier shift. Keep the tone steady and reassuring in every reply, because people often come to us worried about their animals and they need to feel that Aurelia Skyways has things under control. If a booking is already in progress, read the file from the latest update back to the first note so you understand the full story before you act. Treat each journey as shared work, with the desk, the traveler, and the airport team all carrying part of the responsibility.

Use plain language in every contact and avoid guesswork. If a traveler has special handling needs, confirm what is written before you promise anything new. If you are unsure about a detail, pause and check rather than filling the gap with an assumption. Small mistakes can cause stress for the pet and the traveler, so accuracy matters even when the queue is busy. If Isaac Ibrahim, Emil Ramos, or any other traveler needs a follow-up, keep the message short, clear, and respectful. If Daisy or another pet is mentioned, make sure the care notes are passed on with the same attention as any travel document.

During handover, note any pending calls, missing documents, or questions that still need a reply. If a file is sensitive, keep it inside the team and only share it with staff who need it for the next step. Stay calm if the desk gets crowded, and work through the list in order of need so no one is missed. Close the loop on each item before moving to the next one where you can.

At the end of your cover, leave the next shift a neat summary of what is done, what is waiting, and what still needs checking. If anything urgent comes up that you cannot resolve at desk level, contact the senior coordinator or the duty manager right away.
